solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spat mum’s chop out — no need for these?

indicators.note: spat out suggests letters thrown about, so the preceding words are jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: Mum spits out the chop she was eating, and nobody needs to call for medical help.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: if a patient has already spat out the bad food, the hospital equipment is not needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital devices used to empty swallowed poison would be unnecessary once the dangerous meal has been spat back out.

clue.text: Section of flight starts to surge through sky

indicators.note: starts of the two words means take only the opening letter of each

blocks.note: opening letters of surge and through
the sky is the air above us

explanation.surface: An aircraft climbs sharply through the sky in one part of its flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight looks like air travel, which the sky reinforces; here it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is made up of individual steps, so one step is a single section of it.

clue.text: Butterfly operating strangely

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of its usual order, so the word's letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A butterfly is behaving oddly, flying in a peculiar way.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a common European butterfly whose males have bright orange patches at the wing ends.

clue.text: Matriarch lady moving somewhere in London

indicators.note: moving letters shift them out of place into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: An elderly family matriarch is relocating to a new address in London.
explanation.walkthrough: ADMIRALTY ARCH is a large ceremonial archway between Trafalgar Square and The Mall in London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a landmark building in central London, so a deliberately vague description of a place in the capital fits.

clue.text: Male with skills makes suit

blocks.note: the pronoun for a male
arts are skills or crafts; with simply joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A man with tailoring skills makes himself a suit of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Suit suggests clothing, but it is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four card groupings, alongside clubs, diamonds and spades.

clue.text: Illicit burden athlete dealt with

indicators.note: dealt like cards, the letters are shuffled out and given a fresh order

blocks.note: the fodder, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: An athlete is lumbered with some shady burden, perhaps a doping scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Payments made secretly and dishonestly are said to be passed this way, an idiom for illegal dealings.

clue.text: Vessel in first half of canal

indicators.note: only the opening half is kept, so the back half of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the Panama Canal joins the Atlantic and Pacific

explanation.surface: A boat sits partway along a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The canal is a specific one, the Panama Canal; keeping the first three of its six letters leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan is a cooking container, and vessel is a general word for any receptacle holding liquid.

clue.text: Insect let loose after another insect

indicators.note: letting letters loose frees them to fall into a different arrangement
after places the jumbled piece behind the other one in the answer

blocks.note: a bee is another insect
the fodder

explanation.surface: One insect is released to chase down another.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is a hard-winged insect, so the general class word defines it.

clue.text: Warning in the style of Royal Marines

blocks.note: à la is French for in the manner of
standard abbreviation for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A warning delivered the way the Royal Marines would give one.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal or alert telling people of danger, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: Moderately slow poet pursues article

indicators.note: one thing pursuing another comes behind it, so the poet follows in the answer

blocks.note: the indefinite article
Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet

explanation.surface: A poet sluggishly chases after a magazine article.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the tempo marking means at a walking pace, steady and moderately unhurried.

clue.text: Run, say, number on estate?

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
e.g. means for example, as say does

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a quick tally of the number of people living on a housing estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Estate reads as a housing estate, but it is an estate car; the registration number on its plate is called the reg in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Reg is British shorthand for a vehicle registration, the plate identifier displayed on a car such as an estate.

clue.text: Insect crossing black sticky stuff is slowing down

indicators.note: something crossing another spans it, so the insect stretches around the black stuff

blocks.note: a red ant is an insect
tar is black and sticky

explanation.surface: An ant crawling across sticky black tar is held up.
explanation.walkthrough: Insect is not the definition here: the insect is the wordplay, and the answer is defined by its last words.
explanation.definitionFit: A retardant substance delays or hinders a process, as in fire retardant, so it is slowing things down.

clue.text: Plant weapon on source

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it

blocks.note: an arrow is a weapon
the root of something is its origin

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put a weapon on the person who supplied the information.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like a verb, to hide something; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a tropical plant whose starchy tubers are used as a thickener in cooking.

clue.text: Popular, outwardly ethereal holiday venue

indicators.note: outwardly means only the outside, so just the end letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: hot means in demand
first and last letters of ethereal

explanation.surface: A dreamy, otherworldly resort is proving popular with tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a place where travellers stay overnight, often while on vacation.

clue.text: Fear Hard Right, caught between two alternatives

indicators.note: something caught between two others sits in the middle of them

blocks.note: H for hard, as on pencils
or is the word offering an alternative, used twice
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Voters dread the hard right when torn between two political options.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is intense dread or shock, a strong form of being afraid.

clue.text: Nag Romeo, in tights

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: hose is an old word for tights or stockings
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone scolds Romeo for wearing tights, as Shakespeare's hero might on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Nag looks like a verb, to pester, but it is the noun for an old horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old or worn-out horse, so the general word for the animal fits.

clue.text: Measurement of 8 hours to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with points at the first letter only

blocks.note: first letter of hours
the number written as a word

explanation.surface: Someone takes a measurement that runs for eight hours at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Height is how tall something is, one of the standard dimensions you measure.

clue.text: Give Cheeko money in split debt settlement

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a rent is a tear or split
Cheeko is the setter, so the request is to pay me

explanation.surface: The setter demands cash from his split of a debt being paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pen name, so Cheeko is ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Repayment is paying back money borrowed, which settles a debt.

clue.text: Not prepared to retreat in conflict

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: raw means unprepared or uncooked

explanation.surface: Untrained troops are forced to fall back during a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: War is armed fighting between nations, the largest kind of conflict.

clue.text: Classify emotion when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round in a loop, so the last letter comes to the front

blocks.note: anger is an emotion

explanation.surface: Sorting out how you feel while out on a bike ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To range things is to arrange or rank them into groups, so it means classify.

clue.text: Published British newspaper best when boasting

blocks.note: a book that is out has been published
B is the abbreviation for British
a rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A British paper prints a piece in which someone shows off.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbrag someone is to surpass them at bragging, beating them in a contest of self-praise.

clue.text: Perhaps pet test is over

indicators.note: in a down clue, over suggests turning the word upside down

blocks.note: the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for cars

explanation.surface: An exam on looking after a pet has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, and a cat is one example of a household pet, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Famous landscaper’s name on top of hill

indicators.note: the second piece is placed onto the end of the first

blocks.note: the brow is the summit of a hill
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A garden designer's name is carved at the summit of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Capability Brown was the eighteenth-century English designer of country-house parklands such as Blenheim.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot Brown, nicknamed Capability, is the best-known English garden and park designer.

clue.text: PM Heath irate about site for old contest

indicators.note: about suggests being turned around and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, twelve letters

explanation.surface: Former Prime Minister Edward Heath is furious about a planning matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a British Conservative Prime Minister in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Romans staged gladiator fights in open-air oval arenas with tiered seating.
